title: Implement tenant-aware congestion controller and cooperative backpressure protocol for streaming workers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: our existing worker pools (Redis consumers + Kafka stream processors) show poor isolation under multi-tenant noisy neighbors. Spikes from a single tenant cause head-of-line blocking, bursty retry storms, and SLO violations for unrelated customers. Current ad-hoc shed/kill heuristics make rollouts risky and provide little observability into tenant-level congestion.

Goal: introduce a tenant-aware congestion control layer and a cooperative backpressure protocol that: 1) prevents noisy tenants from causing cluster-wide latency spikes, 2) enables graceful shedding and prioritized delivery, and 3) provides transparent operational controls (per-tenant credits, debug endpoints, dashboards).

Scope: this ticket implements the runtime plumbing and migration path for streaming workers:
- Per-tenant credit buckets enforced at ingress (HTTP/gRPC) and at message broker consumers (Redis lists/streams and Kafka consumer groups).
- Cooperative backpressure signals propagated between workers and the ingress/control plane via lightweight lease/heartbeat metadata and a Redis pubsub channel for immediate congestion notifications.
- Token-based admission control: requests consume credits; when exhausted, worker can queue with bounded wait or return a retriable 429 with a backoff header.
- Soft-shed policies: low-priority requests are demoted (e.g., non-critical evals) while high-priority customers retain minimum guaranteed throughput.
- Metrics and tracing: per-tenant queue length, credit utilization, shed-rate, average wait time, and SLO error budget burn rate surfaced in Grafana and linked to alerts.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We use a centralized tenant-state store in Redis (small hash per tenant) to keep credits and soft priorities. This favors operational visibility and fast updates at the cost of one small read/write per admission decision. We mitigate hot-key risk by sharding tenant state and caching recent decisions in-process for 100ms.
- For Kafka consumers we piggyback credit checks on the fetch loop; if tenant credits are low we pause partition processing for that tenant for up to 500ms and attempt cooperative retries. This reduces rebalancing churn vs using consumer pause per partition aggressively.
- Backpressure signaling uses Redis pubsub channel "tenant-congestion" for urgent state changes (e.g., emergency throttle); longer-lived state is persisted in the tenant-state hash. Pubsub is best-effort — we rely on periodic heartbeats to reconcile missed messages.
- To minimize latency regression we perform checks before heavy compute and only read Redis state on misses in the in-memory cache. Admission-path is optimized and benchmarked under synthetic load (see PR notes).

Migration plan:
1) Feature-flag rollout: implement with a runtime flag (congestion.v2.enabled) default off.
2) Canary: enable on a single low-traffic region and measure credit utilization and shed-rate for 48h.
3) Incremental tenant opt-in: start with internal tenants and a set of low-risk customers.
4) Global enable with gradual throttling of very high-volume tenants while support works with customers to tune limits.
5) Fallback: global kill-switch that disables cooperative protocol and falls back to existing behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- No >5% increase in median p95 token generation latency in the canary region when feature-flag enabled for internal traffic.
- Reduction in cross-tenant SLO violation incidents attributed to tenant spikes by >=60% during controlled load tests.
- New Grafana dashboards showing per-tenant credit consumption, shed-rate, and queue latency.
- Automated integration test that simulates noisy neighbor and proves isolation.
- Operational runbook documenting how to tune credit limits, enable/disable tenants, and perform emergency throttles.

Open questions:
- Default credit allocation formula: static per-tenant baseline vs usage-derived proportional baseline. Proposal: start with proportional baseline derived from 30-day average QPS + minimum floor.
- How to handle long-lived streams for clients with sporadic activity (avoid draining credits prematurely). Proposal: separate bucket for streaming keepalive heartbeats.

Related artifacts:

- Benchmark notes and synthetic load scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/tenant-congestion
- Draft runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/queue-op-runbook

Rollout checklist: feature flag gate, integration tests green, canary monitor up, on-call notified, runbook linked, post-rollout incident playbook prepared.

2025-03-01 - Diego Alvarez: Addressed PR feedback. Added integration test that simulates 50 tenants with one noisy tenant; measured 68% reduction in cross-tenant p99 latency compared to baseline in synthetic env. Pushed PR #12345 for review.

2025-03-04 - SRE (Alex Kim): Canary infra prepared. Alert rules added: tenant_credit_depleted_rate > 1% for 5m, and tenant_shed_rate > 0.5% sustained, will page on higher thresholds. Scheduled canary for 2025-03-06.
